BED-05 ships as scoped with the measured limit documented. Whether the program rebuild becomes incremental or moves out of the request path reopens a scoping decision the story took as given, so it belongs to a follow-up story.

D-01 / DATA-DESIGN §5 overclaim ON CONFLICT convergence: proven only for a STATIC usage_events read-set (which is what AC-1's test holds). Under genuinely concurrent different-program ingest, with usage_events still being written during the race, a stale read can silently overwrite a fresher committed aggregate — no exception, no log signal. Self-heals on the next rebuild anywhere in the system and is still better than the shipped crash-on-collision. Correct the wording and record the staleness window as an accepted residual risk; harden later with a scoped pg_advisory_xact_lock around only the org-write critical section if stronger guarantees are wanted.

func.min(user) in _build_user_sessions relies on a session_id -> single user 1:1 invariant that is NOT schema-enforced — the only constraint is UniqueConstraint(program_id, session_id, cmd_ts). No test detects a violation. Not a regression (shipped code had the same gap, less deterministically). Add a cheap data-quality signal.

generate_rollup_golden_snapshots.py seeds one event per session universally, inflating the golden fixtures to ~49MB (dominated by degenerate user_sessions rows) while leaving multi-row session aggregation untested at that scale. Regenerating with ~20-50 events/session would shrink them an order of magnitude and close the coverage gap at once.

Explicit date_trunc(..., 'UTC') diverges from personal_usage.py's un-zoned precedent. Verified sound for this deployment (Docker postgres:16, no TZ override) but the assumption is undocumented — record it in DECISIONS.md / DATA-DESIGN.md.

docs/activity/activity.jsonl's writer mutates several pre-existing historical rows (unrelated /model, AUTH-01, AUTH-03 entries) rather than only appending. Not BED-05 code — harness-hook issue, investigate separately.

Escalation of AF-08-carry: 3,645ms p95 at 40k in-program exceeds ING-02's OWN stated end-to-end p95 <=3s ceiling on its own. Raise as a blocking-dependency note on ING-02's plan rather than reopening BED-05. Reviewer concurs AF-08 should stay carry-forward here, not block.

Security review F-SEC-4 (Low, round 2): _assert_safe_to_truncate() is enforced only in main(); _truncate_all() and _run() remain independently importable and would skip it if ever called another way. Verified no live bypass exists — repo-wide grep shows nothing imports this module, consistent with the scripts/-is-CLI-only precedent (test_mint_ingest_token.py uses subprocess). Recommended defence-in-depth: move the assertion inside _truncate_all() itself. Deliberately NOT applied in this PR: it is a behaviour/structure change, and the implement gate's own rule is that the commit must be the snapshot the gates passed — a post-PASS code edit would mean the security verdict no longer covers the shipped code. Apply it with a gate re-run, or in a follow-up.
